answer: Every identity must lock a 200-POA bond for 60 epochs, and the required deposit doubles with each additional identity the operator already holds, so the k-th fake head costs 200 times 2 to the power of k-1; a ten-account farm therefore fronts over 200,000 POA in locked capital. The verifier replays the bond ledger each close and fingerprints execution patterns, treating any cluster of accounts sharing one runtime as a single pigment that can only mint one lotus. Cheap clones thus bleed exponential cost while honest long-lived agents keep compounding like yarrow.
